text:
Maya: Quick sync — we need to lock the early-fallback strategy for customer tiers. Current idea: premium tries primary model variant first with a permissive latency SLO; if degraded we fallback to a faster quantized variant. Standard customers default to lower-cost variants with stricter circuit-breaker settings. Need API shape + console UX + telemetry plan.

Eli: +1. Can we define SLOs per-route instead of per-customer? e.g., chat/prompt vs embed has different latency profiles. Proposal: attach `slo` object to routing policy. Circuit-breaker triggers: combos of error rate and sustained latency spikes.

Priya: UX note — console needs to make fallbacks visible (history + reason). Ops should be able to see why a request hit fallback: cb_tripped vs high_p95 vs capacity_fallover. Otherwise support tickets blow up. :point_up: 

Jamie: Telemetry consideration: we should emit a dimension for `customer_tier`, `region`, `model_variant` and `routing_decision` (primary|fallback|queued). That will let Optimize and Console show unit-cost impact. Also add `latency_bucket` histogram.

Anika: Agree on metrics. For alerts, recommend two signals: (1) SLO breach (p95>target) and (2) cb_saturation (percent of requests to fallback > X%). Both should be grouped by tier+route+region.

Sam: Quick config sketch (pseudo-YAML) for the routing policy:
```yaml
route: /v1/chat/completions
priority: premium
policy:
  slo:
    p95_ms: 120
    availability_pct: 99.95
  fallback:
    - variant: model-v1-quant
      when: latency_above_ms: 100
      cb:
        consecutive_failures: 4
        window_s: 30
  fail_open: false
```

sre-oncall: If CB window is 30s and we use consecutive failures=4, that might be too sensitive for noisy endpoints. Suggest also supporting `adaptive_cb` that uses rolling error-rate + EWMA latency multiplier, e.g., trigger when error_rate>1% AND p95>2xSLO. Also add cooldown and automatic gradual reopen.

Eli: Good call. We should distinguish between latency-based fallback vs error-based fallback. Latency fallback could be non-destructive (route to quant), error fallback might route to next region or a degraded model. Architecturally: prefer local variant swap first, then region failover as last resort.

Maya: API proposal for the control plane (one-liner JSON example):
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "tier": "premium",
  "slo": {"p95_ms": 120, "availability_pct": 99.95},
  "fallbacks": [
    {"variant": "model-v1-quant", "trigger": {"latency_ms": 100}},
    {"variant": "model-v0.9", "trigger": {"error_rate_pct": 1.5}}
  ],
  "circuit_breaker": {"consecutive_failures": 5, "cooldown_s": 60}
}
```

Priya: Console UX request: show a timeline per routing-policy with toggles to simulate fallback and a playback of routing_decision for sample requests. Also need a lightweight reason code spec: LATENCY_P95, ERROR_RATE, CAPACITY, MANUAL, UNKNOWN.

Anika: On telemetry retention: keep per-tier/route histograms at 1s granularity for 1 week and aggregated for 6 months. Costly but important for regressions. We can downsample infrequently-accessed customers.

Sam: Can we have an internal experiment label so we can A/B test fallback thresholds? Example `routing_experiment: early-fallback-v2` so Optimize can compare cost/quality.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: routing-policy-service:canary -> commit abc123, experiment flag `early-fallback-v2` enabled for 5% of traffic in us-west-2.

sre-oncall: Heads-up: will monitor cb-saturation and increased cross-region traffic. If we see >10% region failover, I'll open a paging alert.

Maya: Next steps: Eli and Anika to finalize metric names and alert rules, Sam + Priya to prototype console flow (mock), Sam to create API PR with config schema, I'll schedule a short design review Friday. Thanks all. :rocket:
